strengths: Meaning lines land as one thought: burnt out -> keep it fed -> steady care -> what needs tending, all true to Li's fire-needs-fuel sense.
Plates suit their lines: the ox at a lit doorway for 'keep it fed', the sun over a walked path for 'steady care, not big gestures'.
End card and credit hold long enough and read clean against the black.

changes.change: Put the hook line over a plate or a scene (a dimmed lamp, a spent match, a screen glowing then fading) instead of plain white text on black.
changes.why: Rubric asks for a real situation readable at a glance in the first 2 s; text alone on black is the weakest visual beat in the short and doesn't stop the scroll as hard as a recognizable scene would.

changes.change: Drop the whip-left/whip-right pair during hook and hexagram (bars 20-23, energy flat at 5-6) and hold a slower push-in instead; keep the whips for the screens section where energy sits at 7.
changes.why: Rubric asks the cut style to suit the energy class; whipping through a steady, low-energy stretch reads busier than the music, and saving the sharper cuts for the higher-energy screens section would make the drop and screens hit harder by contrast.

changes.change: Hold on screen 3 (YOUR DAY, READ) an extra half second or add a short caption naming the changing-line feature ('30 becoming 56'), since that's the most distinct capability shown.
changes.why: The four screens are even in length but not even in how much a first-time viewer can parse; the changing-line/hexagram-to-hexagram idea is the app's most unusual feature and gets the same 3 s as the simpler screens.

review.notes: Confirm the drop actually lands audibly at 14.4 s under the zoom+shake, and that the typewriter reveals on screen 1 and the end card ('READ THE STRUC...', 'REVEAL THE MOME...') read as intentional builds rather than clipped text when watched at speed.
